source.title: Bounds on 2-torsion in class groups of number fields and integral points on elliptic curves

summary: Partial source-critical checkpoint, not a complete extraction. Both available 2017 texts have been read completely; they differ (the February copy adds the degree-one del Pezzo application), and neither has been matched to the 2019 revisions underlying the 2020 article. Twenty foundational/geometry-of-numbers items are checked against pinned declarations and reviewed audits: ten library, one planned, nine missing. The nine missing items are provisionally routed as a Part II of EffectiveBounds. All final torsion, elliptic/hyperelliptic, quartic-count and function-field branches remain to extract after resolving version and hypothesis questions documented in the report. Do not generate accepted routes or mark complete from this checkpoint.

items.name: Ordinary ideal class group
items.statement: For a number field K with ring of integers O_K, Cl(K) is the multiplicative group of nonzero fractional O_K-ideals modulo nonzero principal fractional ideals.
items.locator: Introduction p.1 and §2 p.4, Taniguchi 2017-02-18 copy
items.note: ClassGroup is defined for a domain using invertible fractional ideals; for O_K the Dedekind-domain equivalence supplies the stated carrier. Not the narrow class group.

items.name: Finiteness of the number-field class group
items.statement: For every number field K, the ordinary ideal class group Cl(O_K) is finite; its cardinality is h(K).
items.locator: Introduction p.1, implicit in h_m(K); §6 p.10
items.note: This does not supply a degree-uniform torsion estimate.

items.name: Archimedean absolute values
items.statement: M_infinity(K) consists of absolute values associated to embeddings K → C; at a complex place use the ordinary complex modulus, not its square.
items.note: The product formula gives complex places multiplicity two. Keep that multiplicity in volume/norm computations.

items.name: Integral discriminant and its absolute value
items.statement: For a number field K, discr(K) is the determinant of the trace pairing on an integral basis; it is nonzero and independent of the integral basis. Write D_K = |discr(K)|.
items.note: Despite its docstring, the Lean integer discr is signed. Use its absolute value in all real powers.

items.name: Minkowski space with one complex embedding per pair
items.statement: If K has r real and s complex places, embed K into R^r × C^s via its real embeddings and one representative of each complex pair. The resulting real space has dimension n = [K:Q] = r + 2s.
items.note: Product measure is the unweighted real-coordinate measure. The Euclidean norm used for successive minima needs an explicit compatible norm, not the default product sup norm.

items.name: Covolume of the ring of integers
items.statement: In R^r × C^s with ordinary product Lebesgue measure, the mixed embedding of O_K has covolume 2^(-s) sqrt(D_K).
items.note: Do not use this constant unchanged for the metric which weights complex coordinates by two.

items.name: Covolume of a fractional ideal
items.statement: For a nonzero fractional ideal J of O_K, covol(mixedEmbedding(J)) = N_abs(J) 2^(-s) sqrt(D_K). In particular J = I^(-1) gives 2^(-s) sqrt(D_K)/N(I).
items.note: Lean input is a unit of the fractional-ideal monoid. The inverse case is a specialization plus multiplicativity of absolute norm.

items.name: Minkowski convex-body theorem, strict volume form
items.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real normed space with additive Haar measure μ. Let L be a countable additive subgroup with measurable fundamental domain F. If S is convex, symmetric about zero, and μ(F) 2^(dim E) < μ(S), then S contains a nonzero point of L.
items.note: General library statement read with its actual hypotheses; strict inequality alone does not justify the equality case in Theorem 2.1.

items.name: Minkowski convex-body theorem, compact boundary form
items.statement: In a nontrivial finite-dimensional real normed space with additive Haar measure, a compact convex symmetric set S satisfying μ(F) 2^(dim E) ≤ μ(S) contains a nonzero point of a countable discrete subgroup L with fundamental domain F.
items.locator: §2 p.4, boundary case needed for the displayed non-strict bounds
items.note: Compactness, discreteness and nontriviality are genuine hypotheses; the number-field degree is positive.

items.name: Minkowski ideal-class representative bound
items.statement: Every class c of a degree-n number field of signature (r,s) contains a nonzero integral ideal I with N(I) ≤ (4/pi)^s (n!/n^n) sqrt(D_K).
items.note: Useful existing baseline, but the paper's simultaneous bounds on a generator of I^m are stronger and are not this theorem.

items.name: Successive minima
items.statement: For a full lattice Λ in a positive-dimensional Euclidean real space and its closed unit ball B, λ_i is the infimum of t > 0 for which Λ ∩ tB spans a real subspace of dimension at least i, for 1 ≤ i ≤ n.
items.locator: Theorems 1.6 and 3.1, pp.3,5; explicit expansion of the standard term used there
items.note: Reviewed AUDIT-02 marks the successive-minimum definitions and second theorem absent. No new competing general definition is proposed.

items.name: Weighted box and polydisc for a torsion ideal
items.statement: Given a degree-n number field K, m ≥ 1, a nonzero integral ideal I, and I^m = (α) with α ≠ 0, put R_v = D_K^(1/(2n)) |α|_v^(-1/m). In mixed space take intervals [-R_v,R_v] at real places and closed complex discs of radius R_v. This compact symmetric convex body's volume is 2^r pi^s D_K^(1/2)/N(I).
items.note: Preprint extraction only: both public 2017 copies agree on this section; comparison with the final 2020 text remains open. The displayed preprint volume formula needs dimensional care: a complex disc contributes pi R_v^2, not sqrt(pi) R_v. Its volume is at least 2^n covol(I^(-1)) because pi ≥ 2.

items.name: Small inverse-ideal multiplier
items.statement: With the preceding hypotheses, there exists κ ∈ I^(-1), κ ≠ 0, with |κ|_v ≤ D_K^(1/(2n)) |α|_v^(-1/m) for every infinite place v.
items.note: Preprint extraction only: both public 2017 copies agree on this section; comparison with the final 2020 text remains open. Consume the compact non-strict Minkowski theorem and fractional-ideal covolume, then keep the nonzero witness.

items.name: Archimedean-balanced generator of a torsion representative
items.statement: For a degree-n number field K and an ideal class of order m ≥ 1, there is a nonzero integral ideal J in the class and β ∈ O_K, β ≠ 0, such that J^m = (β) and |β|_v ≤ D_K^(m/(2n)) for every infinite place v.
items.note: Preprint extraction only: both public 2017 copies agree on this section; comparison with the final 2020 text remains open. The proof also works if the class order divides m, but this item preserves the theorem's stated order-m hypothesis. Construct J = κ I, β = α κ^m and prove integrality and class preservation.

items.name: Balanced generator for a 2-torsion class
items.statement: For a degree-n number field K and an ideal class of order two, there is a nonzero integral representative J and nonzero β ∈ O_K with J^2 = (β) and |β|_v ≤ D_K^(1/n) at every infinite place.
items.note: Preprint extraction only: both public 2017 copies agree on this section; comparison with the final 2020 text remains open. The trivial class is handled too by the order-dividing version or directly. Count absolute square norms: N_K/Q(β) can be negative; J^2 only forces |N_K/Q(β)| = N(J)^2.

items.name: Reduced integral basis starting with one
items.statement: For a degree-n number field with n ≥ 2, choose a Z-basis 1,v_1,...,v_(n-1) of O_K, ordered by archimedean Euclidean length, with reduction comparisons |v_i| ≪_n |v| outside the preceding rational span and product |v_1|...|v_(n-1)| asymptotic up to n-dependent positive constants to sqrt(D_K).
items.note: Preprint extraction only: both public 2017 copies agree on this section; comparison with the final 2020 text remains open. Original Siegel proof not read. The sentence prints its comparison only for i ≤ n−2, but the next proof uses it at i=n−1; certify the full reduced-basis lemma, primitive vector 1, metric normalization and n=2 case. Generic reduction stays with GN.1/GN.3.

items.name: Top-coordinate multiplication matrix
items.statement: For n ≥ 3 and the basis 1,v_1,...,v_(n-1), form the symmetric (n−2)-square rational matrix A with entry a_ij the coefficient of v_(n−1) in v_i v_j, 1 ≤ i,j ≤ n−2.
items.note: Preprint extraction only: both public 2017 copies agree on this section; comparison with the final 2020 text remains open. This is a coordinate construction on field multiplication, not the trace Gram matrix.

items.name: Nondegeneracy of the top-coordinate multiplication matrix
items.statement: For any degree-n field extension K/Q, n ≥ 3, and Q-basis 1,v_1,...,v_(n−1), the preceding matrix A has nonzero determinant.
items.note: Preprint extraction only: both public 2017 copies agree on this section; comparison with the final 2020 text remains open. If r in span(v_1,...,v_(n−2)) lies in its kernel, multiplication by r preserves L = span(1,...,v_(n−2)). For r ≠ 0, Q(r) has degree at least two dividing both n and n−1, impossible. Separately extract the nonzero-permutation term in det A.

items.name: Degree-dependent upper bound for the largest minimum
items.statement: For each n ≥ 2 there is C_n > 0 such that every degree-n number field K satisfies λ_n(O_K) ≤ C_n D_K^(1/n), for the ordinary archimedean Euclidean lattice. With a controlled reduced basis as in §3, also |v_(n−1)| ≪_n D_K^(1/n).
items.note: Preprint extraction only: both public 2017 copies agree on this section; comparison with the final 2020 text remains open. The n=2 case follows from the product bound. For n≥3 use a permutation with all a_i,pi(i) nonzero, reduction and multiplicative norm comparison; obtain |v_(n−1)|^n ≪_n D_K. Constants are degree-dependent.

items.name: Coarse count of small algebraic integers
items.statement: For a fixed degree n and fixed positive archimedean scale c, the number of β ∈ O_K satisfying |β|_v ≤ c D_K^(1/n) at every infinite place is O_(n,c)(D_K^(1/2)), uniformly over degree-n number fields K.
items.note: Preprint extraction only: both public 2017 copies agree on this section; comparison with the final 2020 text remains open. Use the reduced basis and largest-minimum estimate to fit a fundamental parallelepiped inside a fixed dilation of the box; then a disjoint-translate volume argument. Not an automatic consequence of fixed-lattice asymptotics. Square-norm savings are not extracted in this checkpoint.

prerequisites.citation: C. L. Siegel, Lectures on the Geometry of Numbers, Lecture X §6 (1989 edition).
prerequisites.why: Reduced basis with initial vector 1, product estimate and the last-index comparison used in §3. Original source not read; exact normalization and proof are still required. The link is to the citing author's bibliography, not an accessed copy of Siegel.

prerequisites.citation: E. Bombieri and J. Pila, The number of integral points on arcs and ovals, Duke Mathematical Journal 59 (1989), 337–357, Theorem 5.
prerequisites.why: Coefficient-uniform curve bound used in §4. Original theorem not read in this checkpoint; verify weighted rectangle, total degree, squarefree-part degree, and both norm signs. The link is to the citing author's bibliography, not an accessed copy of Bombieri–Pila.

prerequisites.citation: H. A. Helfgott and A. Venkatesh, Integral points on elliptic curves and 3-torsion in class groups, JAMS 19 (2006), 527–550.
prerequisites.why: Theorem 3.8 and Corollaries 3.9/3.11 supply packing/height estimates in §§5.1 and 5.4. Not read in this checkpoint; the del Pezzo application needs the height-sensitive version, not only total integral points.

prerequisites.citation: A. Brumer and K. Kramer, The rank of elliptic curves, Duke Mathematical Journal 44 (1977), 715–743, Proposition 7.1 and following remark.
prerequisites.why: Explicit 2-Selmer dimension bound through the cubic étale algebra. Not read; audit discriminant versus ramification support and reducible algebras. The link is to the citing author's bibliography, not an accessed copy of Brumer–Kramer.

prerequisites.citation: J. Tsimerman, Brauer–Siegel for arithmetic tori and lower bounds for Galois orbits of special points, JAMS 25 (2012), 1091–1117, Lemma 6.1.
prerequisites.why: Quartic/cubic-resolvent class-group 2-torsion comparison, including the paper's extension to reducible étale resolvents. Not read; verify exact hypotheses before importing.

prerequisites.citation: A. Sedunova, On the Bombieri–Pila method over function fields, arXiv:1506.08757v1, Theorem 1.
prerequisites.why: The omitted details of the bounded-gonality branch in §7 require its exact uniformity, characteristic and degree hypotheses. Not read.

prerequisites.citation: A. M. Baily (1980); H. Cohn (1954); M. Bhargava and A. Shnidman (2014); H. Cohen and A. Morra (2011), works cited in §6.
prerequisites.why: Future extraction must split Baily's resolvent-weighted estimate, cyclic cubic asymptotic, fixed-quadratic-resolvent cubic asymptotic and partial summation. This is an acquisition checklist, not verified statements or an assertion that every such input lacks an atlas owner.

routes.title: Effective arithmetic bounds and geometry of numbers, Part II: class-group torsion and balanced ideal generators
routes.reason: The completed roadmap provides coarse effective class-number/ideal bounds and geometry-of-numbers infrastructure, but not balanced generators or this degree-dependent largest-minimum theorem. Preserve its existing work. This checkpoint proposes only the extracted foundation, not yet the final paper's full torsion programme.
routes.brief: Provisional checkpoint brief; resolve source-version agreement before design intake. Build on Effective arithmetic bounds and geometry of numbers (tauceti:Completed/EffectiveBounds), importing its existing packing and class-number APIs. Import mixed embeddings, fractional-ideal covolumes and the compact Minkowski theorem from the pinned Mathlib baseline; import general successive minima and reduced-basis theory from Geometry of numbers and quadratic arithmetic (GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic), especially GN.1/GN.3, rather than duplicating them. For a degree-n number field and an order-m ideal class prove existence of an integral representative J with J^m=(β) and |β|_v≤D_K^(m/(2n)) for every infinite place. Prove the m=2 specialization and λ_n(O_K)≪_n D_K^(1/n), via the nonsingular top-coordinate multiplication matrix, including n=2 separately. Export the O_n(D_K^(1/2)) balanced-box count. Give each construction an API, proof dependency and tests (Q, real quadratic, imaginary quadratic, degree three); preserve complex-place dimension factors and norm signs. Extend this brief with the paper's actual final torsion bounds only after completing §§4–7 extraction and the unresolved published-version/prerequisite checks.
